The paths above are the surfaces that REPRODUCE it: the five kept pins' `mechanism` keys in config/GUNE5D/webfrank.json each quote their three probed forms with measured word counts and body hashes; `probe.py <unit> <fn> --raw --ops` is the arbiter every one of the eighteen probes used; `fnasm.py <unit> <fn> --diff --raw` is the aligned view clause (2)'s screen is read from; `wf_word_diff.py` supplies the differing-word counts; and `savedregs.py`'s own docstring is the evidence for the scope paragraph, since it reads callee-saved registers only. The two attempt records carrying the positive and the flip are attempt.WR_missilecollideenemy-promoted-at-source-by-sinking-one-initialiser-and-its-rule-deleted.20260904.v1 and attempt.WR_fn800c03e0-two-more-class-boundaries-discharge-the-withhold-and-the-rule-ships-flipping-dbgtext.20260904.v1.
attributes.falsifier: A volatile-register residual on a window whose two streams already agree in opcode and LOAD ORDER, closed by a declaration-order or declaration-class edit alone with the surrounding statement order held fixed, would refute clause (1). A pin whose value-producing statements are already in the target's order and which nevertheless closes on an adjacent transposition would refute clause (2). A leaf function of the shape in clause (3) -- every value a compile-time constant consumed by a global store -- whose object bytes MOVE under any local-variable edit refutes clause (3); the check is `probe.py <unit> <fn> --raw --ops` reporting a body hash different from the clean baseline's.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
MWCC GC 1.2.5 family, per-TU flags as in configure.py. THREE CLAUSES ABOUT THE **VOLATILE** REGISTER BANKS (GPR r0/r3-r12 and FPR f0-f13), which the existing declaration-order corpus does not cover and has been repeatedly misapplied to.

SCOPE AND STANDING FIRST, because this is a boundary as much as a law. claim.law.MV_callee-saved-numbering-has-a-width-class-ahead-of-declaration-order.20260902.v1, claim.law.SP_initializer-presence-outranks-declaration-position-in-callee-saved-numbering.20260901.v1 and claim.law.initialised-accumulator-pair-order-selects-register-per-pair.20260831.v1 are all about CALLEE-SAVED numbering, and savedregs.py -- the tool the corpus reaches for -- reads callee-saved registers ONLY, by its own docstring. A residual sitting in volatile scratch is therefore invisible to that whole apparatus, and reaching for those three laws on one is a category error that costs probes. Measured this run: on MissileCollideEnemy the callee-saved f29/f30/f31 agreed in both streams throughout while the entire four-word residual lived in f0-f5, and the declaration-class probe those laws predict (converting a declaration-initializer into an assignment) measured NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, moving nothing.

(1) VOLATILE SCRATCH IS NUMBERED IN THE ORDER THE VALUES ARE PRODUCED, NOT IN DECLARATION ORDER. Where two streams agree on opcode and load ORDER inside a window and differ only in which volatile register holds which value, the assignment follows the order of the STATEMENTS that produce those values. On MissileCollideEnemy the block's loads are emitted in the order its assignments appear, and their scratch numbers are handed out in that same order.

(2) SO THE LEVER IS TRANSPOSING AN ADJACENT PAIR OF ASSIGNMENTS, AND IT IS CHEAP. Transposing exactly one adjacent pair -- `enemyRadius = radius + PF(enemy, offsetof(Enemy, rad), f32);` moved above `dz = PF(enemy, offsetof(Enemy, objgrp.coll_pos[2]), f32) - to[2];` -- took MissileCollideEnemy from 4 raw differing words to 0 and let its rule be deleted. The block's other four assignments were ALREADY in the target's order, so the whole residual came from one pair written the wrong way round, and nothing in the diff pointed at source order: it reads as pure allocator noise, which is precisely why a postprocessor rule had been authored for it. AN ENABLING SPELLING IS OFTEN NEEDED AND IS NOT ITSELF THE LEVER: the first of the two values was a declaration-initializer, which must become a plain assignment before it can be transposed at all, and that split ALONE measured NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL. Report the pair as one lever whose byte-visible half is the order. THE SCREEN, before any probe: list the block's assignments in source order, list the target's load order from `fnasm.py <unit> <fn> --diff --raw`, and look for a transposed adjacent pair. If the two streams' load orders DIFFER, this is not the mechanism -- the lever only applies where the schedule already agrees and only the homes differ.

(3) TWO PLACES WHERE IT PROVABLY DOES NOT REACH, both measured, both worth screening out before spending a probe. (a) A LEAF WHOSE EVERY VALUE IS A COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT CONSUMED BY A GLOBAL STORE HAS NO SOURCE SURFACE AT ALL. On dbgTextInit (6 insns, a clean f0<->f3-style g0<->g3 involution over three global stores) three probes -- introducing a named local for the single-use constant, giving the SHARED zero carrier its own symbol, and both with declaration order varied -- ALL folded away before codegen at ONE identical body hash, 397bcd36ef10. On sysClearFlags (4 insns) three probes in the statement-shape and named-temporary classes did the same at hash 204b96a5fea6. The front end folds a named local back into its constant before the allocator sees a symbol, so the local-variable class in its entirety -- introduction, carrier splitting AND declaration order -- is unreachable there. This BOUNDS claim.law.variable-identity-reopens-address-pre-and-zero-copy.20260831.v1: its practical rule ('enumerate the shared carriers and give each its own symbol') needs a carrier that SURVIVES folding -- an induction variable, a pointer view, a loop-carried offset -- and a constant does not qualify. (b) ADDING A LOCAL TO A FUNCTION WITH FP TEMPORARIES IS FRAME-TAXED AND USUALLY COSTS MORE THAN THE RESIDUAL. Measured twice on two different TUs in one run: DmgFxAdd 4 raw words -> 13 and InitAnim 4 -> 17, and in BOTH cases the residual left the recolourable class entirely -- probe reported `RECOLOR-SHAPED BUT NOT RECOLOURABLE`, with 7 and 13 IMMEDIATE words respectively sitting outside every register slot -- because the extra f64 slot moves the frame and every frame-relative displacement with it. So a carrier split that needs a NEW declaration is a different and much more expensive proposition than one that reuses an existing symbol, and the two should never be quoted as the same lever.

PRACTICAL ORDERING for a volatile-register recolor: (i) confirm the load orders agree; (ii) try adjacent-statement transposition, reusing existing symbols; (iii) try carrier splitting only where an existing symbol can absorb the role; (iv) treat any probe that adds a declaration as frame work and expect to pay for it; (v) do not probe at all where clause (3a) applies.
